# `scanned/` — image-only PDF with one deliberately low-confidence page

**Manifest id:** `scanned-po-88214` · **File:** `scanned-po-88214.pdf` · **Status:** AUTHORED — generated by `../../../tools/generate_corpus.py`

## Retrieval property exercised

Two things, and they are separate:

1. **OCR text is retrievable at all.** A page with no text layer must go through OCR and end up
   in the index with its part codes intact. `e-004` asks for a code that exists only as pixels.
2. **The OCR warning path fires.** Page 3 is degraded on purpose so it trips the low-confidence
   assessment and the source lands **Ready with warnings**, not Failed and not silently Ready.
   §8.11 requires the warning; §13.7 makes partial OCR a configurable success.

## What the fixture must contain

A **4-page image-only PDF** — scanned or rendered-then-rasterised, with **no text layer on any
page**. A PDF with a hidden text layer skips OCR entirely and this fixture measures nothing.

Content: a purchase order from the fictional customer **Harbourline Water Authority**.

| Page | Quality | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Clean, 300 dpi, straight | PO header: PO number **PO-88214**, dated **2026-02-11**, buyer Harbourline Water Authority, buyer reference `HWA-CAPEX-26-004`. |
| 2 | Clean, 300 dpi, straight | Line items: **2 × KW-1100-B**, unit price 9,200 EUR, total 18,400 EUR. Delivery address, **Dock 7, Harbourline Depot, Fairmont**. |
| 3 | **DELIBERATELY DEGRADED** | Terms and conditions boilerplate, plus a **repeat** of the delivery address. See below. |
| 4 | Clean, 300 dpi, straight | Signature block, "Authorised by: A. Quill, Procurement Lead" (fictional), dated 2026-02-11. |

### Page 3, specifically

Degrade it in ways a real bad scan is degraded, not by blurring uniformly:

- **3° skew** (exercises deskew, and sits above Leptonica's 0.1° floor),
- low contrast — grey text on grey, roughly 35% of full black,
- heavy JPEG artefacting at low quality,
- a faint carbon-copy ghost offset by a few pixels,
- one horizontal fold line crossing two text lines.

**Target:** **both** OCR warning signals fire on page 3, and neither fires on any clean page.
Which statistics those signals read, and at what thresholds, belong to `ocr-pipeline` /
`ingestion-engineer` — they are *recorded* here and never set here. Record the achieved numbers
in this README when the fixture is authored, and degrade for **margin** rather than for
proximity: a page that lands a hair on the firing side of a threshold today and a hair on the
other side after an engine upgrade turns the warning test into a coin flip, and the fix for
that is more degradation, never a lower threshold.

The statistics named in this section changed on 2026-08-07 and the fixture did not. Read
"The mean-confidence floor is real; the mechanism this file used to name was not" below before
using any number here.

### Achieved, measured 2026-08-07 against rapidocr 3.9.2 (PP-OCRv6, onnxruntime)

| Page | Boxes | Mean confidence | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (clean) | 10 | 0.9608 | 1.0134 |
| 2 (clean) | 10 | 0.9947 | 1.1126 |
| **3 (degraded)** | **5** | **0.8291** | **0.1965** |
| 4 (clean) | 4 | 0.9964 | 0.7692 |

Both columns are **fixture-only diagnostics kept for the historical record**, not the shipped
signals. `Mean confidence` is superseded for the reason below; `Coverage` here is recovered
characters over the pre-rasterisation ground truth, whitespace excluded, which only a generator
that authored the page can compute — see "The trap for whoever writes the next fixture".
Coverage above 1.0 on the clean pages is bullet glyphs and misread punctuation adding
characters; it is not a defect. The numbers the warning path actually reads are in
"The replacement statistics" below.

### The mean-confidence floor is real; the mechanism this file used to name was not

**CORRECTED 2026-08-07, after `ingestion-engineer` finished investigating the finding this
fixture produced. The fixture did not change and must not change. `ink = 0.150` ships exactly
as measured above; the bytes, the digest, the manifest and `samples/VERSION` are all
untouched. What was wrong was the *statistic read off the page* and the *mechanism* both this
README and `ocr-pipeline` attributed the floor to.**

The sweep below is kept because it is real data and because it is what forced the correct
diagnosis. It is evidence for a **mechanism**; it was previously written up as a **verdict on
achievability**, and that verdict is now wrong. Holding JPEG, blur and noise and sweeping ink
alone:

| ink | mean confidence | coverage | boxes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.170 | 0.8587 | 0.5447 | 13 |
| 0.160 | 0.8215 | 0.4137 | 10 |
| 0.155 | 0.8141 | 0.2859 | 7 |
| **0.150** | **0.8291** | **0.1965** | **5** (shipped) |
| 0.140 | 0.8826 | 0.1102 | 3 |
| 0.125 | 0.9911 | 0.0415 | 2 |

**What the sweep shows, and it still holds.** Mean confidence never falls below **~0.81** while
any text is still detected. It is not monotone in degradation — it *rises* below `ink = 0.150`,
reaching 0.9911 at the point where two boxes survive. Below that the detector proposes nothing
at all and the mean is 0.0 over an empty set, which is the different condition "no text on this
page" and must never be read as low confidence. `ingestion-engineer` reproduced page 3's
`box_mean = 0.8291` to four decimals and confirmed the floor holds across **five independent
degradation axes** — ink, defocus blur, render resolution, JPEG quantisation and additive
noise — on a second page shape. The floor is a property of the engine, not of this page.

**What the sweep does not show, and the mechanism this file has now named wrong twice.** The
conclusion below has survived both corrections unchanged; the explanation under it has not, so
both superseded versions are recorded rather than quietly replaced.

The *first* attribution was the recognition head's softmax saturating, so a box the detector
proposed is a box the recogniser reads confidently and the mean is computed over survivors.
That was a guess shared by this file and by `ocr-pipeline`, and it was wrong. The *second* was
`rapidocr/main.py:176`, the unconditional drop of boxes whose recognition returned empty. That
one was measured, but by a script that called `engine.text_det()` directly and so bypassed the
`preprocess_img` step `RapidOCR.__call__` runs before detection — **the detector was reading an
input the real pipeline never feeds it.** It is also where the earlier `weak_frac = 0.000`
figure came from, so "the score filter deletes nothing" was accidentally rather than properly
evidenced; it survives re-measurement, at one box on 2 of 14 pages.

Instrumented through the real entry point, `EMPTY_DROPPED` is **0 on 13 of 14 pages** —
including every page of this fixture. The empty-box filter is real and rare, not the mechanism.

**Almost all the loss is at detection.** The detector simply proposes fewer regions as the page
degrades — 15 → 6 → 3 → 1 → 0 — and nothing downstream removes them. Counted at all three
stages on the shipped fixture:

| Page | detector proposed | after empty-drop | after `text_score` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (clean) | 10 | 10 | 10 |
| 2 (clean) | 10 | 10 | 10 |
| **3 (degraded)** | **5** | **5** | **5** |
| 4 (clean) | 4 | 4 | 4 |

All three counts are equal on every row, which is why the `boxes` column in the tables above is
unambiguous: on this fixture it is the detector count, the survivor count and the final count at
once. The `13` at `ink = 0.170` and the `5` at `ink = 0.150` are correct as written.

So on this engine **degradation is expressed as absence, not as low confidence** — the load-
bearing claim, unchanged through two wrong explanations, and *better* supported by this one:
the selection happens **before recognition runs at all**, so no statistic over recogniser
confidence can possibly undo it. That is stronger and more general than "the mean cannot
reach 0.75".

### The replacement statistics, and the fixture passing under them unchanged

`ingestion-engineer` replaced both signals. Recorded here, owned there:

- **`ocr_low_confidence`** — the share of OCR **characters** sitting in cells below a per-cell
  trust floor. Fires when that mass exceeds 0.30, with the floor at 0.80. Character mass, not
  a mean over boxes, is what survives the empty-drop above.
- **`ocr_low_coverage`** — **ink-in-box**: foreground ink inside OCR cell rects over all
  foreground ink on the page. Fires below 0.30.

Both fire on page 3 and neither fires on a clean page, on this fixture's **existing** bytes:

```
page 1: mass=0.1019 coverage=1.0000  -> []
page 2: mass=0.0000 coverage=0.9933  -> []
page 3: mass=0.6161 coverage=0.2070  -> ['ocr_low_confidence:0.62', 'ocr_low_coverage:0.21']
page 4: mass=0.0000 coverage=0.9113  -> []
```

**So the joint target is met, and it was met all along.** The page was never the problem. Do
not degrade it further; the reason `ink = 0.150` was chosen has not changed — 0.207 sits well
clear of the 0.30 line, so an engine upgrade that reads somewhat better does not flip the
fixture, and `0.155` was rejected at 0.2859 because that is exactly the coin flip this section
warns about. The per-box distribution behind the character mass is unchanged too: at the
shipped setting **3 of the 5 boxes read below 0.8 and the worst reads 0.69**.

### The trap for whoever writes the next fixture

**A fixture generator can measure things the pipeline never can, and a threshold calibrated
against one of those numbers is calibrated against nothing.**

The `Coverage` column in the tables above is *recovered characters over pre-rasterisation
ground-truth characters, whitespace excluded*. This corpus can compute it only because it
**generated** the page and therefore knows what was on it. Production has an image and nothing
else, and can never compute it for a real tenant's scan. A number no production code path can
produce is a fixture-only diagnostic, and it must never be the thing a shipped threshold is set
against — which is what the superseded text above was heading towards.

The obvious substitute is wrong, and wrong in the dangerous direction. Box-area over page-area
scores the **clean** signature block at **0.0150**, *below* the **degraded** page at **0.0209**
— so a warning gated on it fires on page 4 and stays quiet on page 3, exactly inverted, with
every number looking plausible. Ink-in-box reproduces the ground-truth measurement without
needing the ground truth: **0.207 against this README's measured 0.1965** on page 3, and
1.000 / 0.993 / 0.911 on the clean pages. That agreement is why it replaced the coverage column
as the shipped signal, and it is the only reason a fixture-only number was allowed to inform a
production one at all.

**The same trap has a second form, and it is the one that produced the wrong mechanism above.**
Instrumenting an engine's *sub-stage* directly — `engine.text_det(rgb)` rather than the entry
point — bypasses the preprocessing the real pipeline applies, so the numbers describe a
pipeline that does not exist. It is the identical error as measuring against ground truth the
pipeline never has: a measurement that is only available from a position production never
occupies. A fixture author is precisely the person most likely to reach for `text_det`
directly, which is why it is written down here as well as in `app/ingestion/ocr/guarded.py`.
Measure through the entry point, or state plainly which stage you bypassed.

> **Finding for `ingestion-engineer` / `ocr-pipeline` — RESOLVED 2026-08-07, recorded because
> the correction matters more than the original.** This file previously reported that a
> low-confidence warning gated on *mean* confidence below 0.75 could never fire on this engine
> at any level of degradation, and proposed a percentile or per-box rule. The observation was
> correct and reproducible; the diagnosis was not, and the suggested fix was directionally
> right for the wrong reason. Degradation on this engine is **absence**, and it happens at
> detection — before recognition runs, so before any confidence statistic exists at all. Per-box
> and percentile rules over recogniser confidence therefore fail for the same reason the mean
> does. The shipped resolution is character mass below a per-cell floor, plus ink-in-box.
> Neither the thresholds nor the fixture are `rag-eval-engineer`'s to change, and neither was
> changed.

The `notes` block for `scanned-po-88214` in `../../manifest.toml` was corrected in the same
change and now agrees with this file. It carries the summary; this file carries the evidence.

Re-measure whenever the OCR engine, its version, or the render DPI changes:

```sh
python tools/generate_corpus.py --out corpus/documents   # regenerate, digests must not move
# then run the measurement described in samples/README.md § Regenerating the fixtures
```

## The rule that keeps this fixture from making the suite flaky

**No golden case may depend on text that appears only on page 3.**

That is why page 3 carries boilerplate and a *repeat* of the delivery address rather than a
unique fact. OCR output on a deliberately-terrible page is not stable across engine versions,
DPI changes, or preprocessing tweaks; a case grading against it would fail for reasons that have
nothing to do with retrieval quality. The warning path is asserted by the **ingestion** test
suite (`pytest-ai-service`), which can read the warning directly. The evaluation suite asserts
only that the *clean* pages are retrievable, and it must stay that way.

The payment terms deliberately live on page 1, not page 3, for the same reason.

## What the fixture must NOT contain

- No real customer, no real address, no real signature, no real PO number format belonging to an
  actual organisation.
- **No 2025-dated order and no second purchase order.** PO-88214 is the only PO in the corpus, so
  a question about Harbourline's ordering history has exactly one true answer and any claim about
  a prior year is ungrounded.
